title: Deep learning from a control vantage point
abstract: arXiv:2610.14385v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This article offers an overview of recent developments in deep learning from a control vantage point. It reviews several classes of models including feedforward and residual neural networks, transformers, large-language models, and selective state space models while explaining how control theory plays an important role in understanding their training, properties, or architecture design. The article explains how residual neural networks can be interpreted as the discretization of a continuous-time control system thereby enabling the use of control theoretic techniques for its analysis. translated_title: 从控制视角看深度学习
translated_abstract: 本文从控制理论的视角综述了深度学习领域的最新进展。文章回顾了包括前馈神经网络、残差神经网络、Transformer、大语言模型以及选择性状态空间模型在内的几类模型，并阐释了控制理论在理解这些模型的训练、性质或架构设计中所起的重要作用。文章解释了残差神经网络可以被解读为连续时间控制系统的离散化，从而使控制理论技术能够用于对其进行分析。为了展示控制与深度学习之间这一桥梁的强大作用，文章讨论了两个技术性结果：1) 残差神经网络逼近任意连续函数的能力是一个非标准的能控性问题，可以利用几何非线性控制方法加以解决；2) Transformer，作为大多数……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文从控制理论视角综述深度学习最新进展，指出残差神经网络可视为连续时间控制系统的离散化，并将其通用逼近能力归结为一个可由几何非线性控制解决的非标准能控性问题。
en_tdlr: This paper surveys recent advances in deep learning from a control-theoretic vantage point, showing that residual neural networks can be interpreted as discretizations of continuous-time control systems and that their universal approximation capability amounts to a non-standard controllability problem solvable via geometric nonlinear control.
